title.title: Fujita's freeness conjecture
title.subtitle: Claim: on every smooth projective $n$-fold, $K_X + mL$ is globally generated for all $m \ge n+1$

plain: Add enough copies of a positive bundle and you can steer sections through any point you like

object.axisLabel: the factor $c$ in $m \ge c\,n$, for large $n$

beats.text: Fujita: adding $n+1$ copies of any ample $L$ to $K_X$ gives a base-point-free bundle
Known up to dimension 5; the best general bound was linear, about $1.78\,n$
The claim is the sharp bound, in a 25-page paper

steps: To free a point, build a divisor that is singular right there
Keep its singular centre under control without losing positivity
A vanishing theorem then lifts a section through the point

achievement.label: Fujita's freeness conjecture (1987)
statement: K_X + mL \text{ globally generated for all } m \ge n+1
achievement.context: Before: dimensions up to 5; in general about $1.78\,n$, after Angehrn–Siu's quadratic bound
achievement.note: Freeness only; Fujita's very-ampleness conjecture is not claimed

verify.detail: No Lean; a previously announced proof by Chan was withdrawn
verify.ourCheck: We graded the claim, not whether it is right

voice.text: K plus m L should be globally generated once m reaches n plus one.
Build a divisor singular at the point, control its centre, then lift a section.
Claimed: the sharp bound, in every dimension.

sources.quote: Han (recent preprint, as cited) m ≥ ⌈1.776 n⌉
Fujita conjectured in 1987 that for a smooth projective $n$-fold and any ample $L$, the bundle $K_X+mL$ is globally generated for $m\ge n+1$.
It was known up to dimension 5
In general the best bound was linear, around $1.78\,n$ in a recent preprint, after Angehrn–Siu's quadratic bound
The paper claims the sharp $n+1$ in 25 pages.
It covers only freeness, not Fujita's very-ampleness conjecture.
I graded what each family claims, not whether it is right.
